title: BOSON-1: Understanding and Enabling Physically-Robust Photonic Inverse Design with Adaptive Variation-Aware Subspace Optimization
problem: Nanophotonic inverse design structures discovered via adjoint methods are numerically plausible but difficult to fabricate and highly sensitive to physical variations. Discrete material distributions create numerous local optima, causing gradient-based methods to converge suboptimally.
motivation: Photonic inverse design enables compact, high-performance device topologies beyond analytic methods, but practical manufacturability and robustness to fabrication variations severely limit deployment.
method: BOSON-1 approaches nanophotonic inverse design as a discrete optimization problem where each location is either solid material or empty space, respecting real constraints of fabrication and real-world variations. To find reliable designs, it combines three strategies: enhanced gradient flows (strong steering toward the goal) to escape local optima (solutions that are locally best but globally poor), restriction of the search to physically fabricable designs, and adaptive sampling-based robust optimization that tests designs under realistic fabrication conditions.
key_novelty: BOSON-1 achieves robust photonic inverse design by restricting the search to fabricable structures and using adaptive sampling-based optimization to find designs that work reliably despite fabrication variations.
contributions: Fabricable photonic structures with 74.3% post-fabrication performance improvement
Adaptive sampling reduces prohibitive runtime for variation robustness
Gradient-based optimization directly in fabricable subspace
primary_theme: Fabrication-aware photonic inverse design with variation robustness
